ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r1.claim: A history of Ibn Abi Khaythama records Adam being called a prophet spoken to, supporting direct speech to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r1.anchor: أنه عليه السلام سئل عن آدم فقال: نبي مكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r2.claim: The majority say the call came through revelation; they cite Moses’ unique distinction as God’s interlocutor and the intercession report, while another passage can be reconciled by limiting Moses’ distinction to earthly speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r2.anchor: وقال الجمهور: إن النداء كان بواسطة الوحي ويؤيده أن موسى عليه السلام هو الذي خص من بين العالم بالكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r3.claim: A view says the call was addressed literally to Adam alone, since no report says God spoke to Eve; a call may address someone by name, kind, or description even when unstated here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r3.anchor: وقيل: النداء لآدم على الحقيقة ولم يرو قط أن الله كلم حواء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r4.claim: The quoted question is grammatically governed by an omitted saying verb and serves as reproach, drawing attention to their oversight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r4.anchor: والجملة معمولة لقول محذوف أي قائلا: ألم أنهكما وهو استفهام معناه العتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r5.claim: The near demonstrative was used when the tree was accessible and eating permitted, while the distant form at reproach intimates the coming separation and expulsion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r5.anchor: ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة إشارة لطيفة حيث كان مباحا له الأكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r6.claim: The reminder that God had told them of Satan’s enmity refers to the earlier warning that he must not cause their expulsion; this is the covenant Adam forgot on the literal sense of forgetting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r6.anchor: وأقل لكما إشارة إلى قوله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan’s enmity was evident because he had refused to prostrate and threatened to mislead Adam’s descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس بين العداوة حيث أبى السجود وقال لأقعدن لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r8.claim: A report says God asked Adam whether the abundance of other trees had not sufficed; Adam says he thought no creature would swear falsely by God, and God then sends him to earn his subsistence through labor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r8.anchor: روي أنه تعالى قال لآدم: ألم يكن لك فيما منحتك من شجر الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r9.claim: The report continues that Adam learned ironwork and farming, then plowed, irrigated, harvested, threshed, winnowed, kneaded, and baked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r9.anchor: وعلم صنعة الحديد وأمر بالحرث فحرث وسقى وحصد ودرس وذر وعجن وخبز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r10.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r10.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy says, Did you not both refrain from that tree, and were you not told?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي ألم تنهيا عن تلكما الشجرة وقيل لكما

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.claim: Verses 11–27 recount Adam's creation, temptation, and expulsion from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.anchor:
the story of Adam’s creation, temptation, and exile from
the Garden.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.claim: Though God accepted Adam and Eve’s repentance, divine wisdom sent them from Paradise to earth for a contest against Satan and his progeny; Paradise became the reward for those who prevail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.anchor: the contest was the same which Ibl īs had challenged them for; however, its locus was shifted from Paradise to earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.claim: The phrase “enemies of one another” casts Adam and Iblīs as opposing parties: Satan may lead Adam’s descendants astray, while they can regain Paradise by defeating his designs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.anchor: Adam (sws) and Ibl īs were sent in this world as two disputing parties.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r43.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r43.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r43.claim: The order to go forth (ukhruj) differs from the later order to descend (ahbitū), which addresses Iblis, Adam, and his wife together and marks their descent from the celestial realm.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r43.anchor: issued to Iblīs, Adam, and his wife collectively in v. 24

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.claim: The command to descend is widely taken to address Adam, Eve and their descendants, as well as Iblis.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r78.anchor: is widely considered to be addressed to Adam and Eve and their future progeny as well as to Iblīs, or Satan (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r79.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r79.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r79.claim: This descent means banishment from the celestial realm, unlike Iblis’s earlier expulsion from the Garden alone.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r79.anchor: The command is taken to indicate their banishment from the celestial realm altogether and is thus different from God’s earlier command banishing Iblīs from the Garden specifically

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r80.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r80.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r80.claim: Some Sufis see the fall as providential and merciful: it led Adam and Eve to earthly vicegerency and created the possibility of drawing near to God through distance and exile.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r80.anchor: Some Sufi commentators emphasize the providential and even merciful aspect of the fall of Adam and Eve

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r81.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r81.speaker: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r81.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh teaches that disobedience producing humility and need is better than obedience producing might and pride.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r81.anchor: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh, an eighth-/fourteenth-century Shādhilī Sufi master, said in his book al-Ḥikam

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r82.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r82.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r82.claim: The fall lets God manifest forgiveness and lets Adam, and humanity through him, manifest humility, repentance, and return to God, attaining perfection unavailable without the fall.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r82.anchor: the fall affords God the opportunity to manifest His Attribute of Forgiveness and offers Adam, and by extension all human beings, the possibility of manifesting humility and repentance

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r83.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r83.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r83.claim: Mustaqarr, rendered “dwelling place,” means a settled or established place; 6:98 discusses the term further.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r83.anchor: Dwelling place translates mustaqarr, meaning a settled or established place;

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r84.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r84.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r84.claim: Earthly life’s temporary enjoyment is repeated elsewhere and is contrasted throughout the Quran with the lasting full reward or punishment of the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r84.anchor: The idea that earthly life entails enjoyment for a while is repeated in various ways elsewhere in the Quran

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the interpretation of اهبطوا was already given in the account in al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r7.anchor: قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين تقدم تفسير هذا في البقرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r1.speaker: كثير من السلف
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r1.claim: Many early authorities take the command as addressed to Adam, Eve, and Iblīs; its repetition to Iblīs may show he remains bound up with humankind in earthly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r1.anchor: كثير من السلف أنه خطاب لآدم وحواء عليهما السلام وابليس عليه اللعنة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r2.claim: Alternatively, the command may have been issued separately and summarized, as in the address to the messengers to eat good things.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r2.anchor: الأمر وقع مفرقا وهذا نقل له بالمعنى وإجمال له

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the address to include Adam, Eve, and their descendants, thereby addressing those not yet existent.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r3.anchor: الفراء كونه خطابا لهما ولذريتهما وفيه خطاب المعدوم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r4.claim: Some take it to address only Adam and Eve, since the same story says ‘both of you descend’; the plural can stand for descendants because they are humanity’s source.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r4.anchor: لهما فقط لقوله سبحانه ( قال اهبطا منها جميعا )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r5.claim: Another view includes Adam, Eve, Iblīs, and the serpent, with objections and answers already discussed in Sūrat al-Baqara.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r5.anchor: لهما ولابليس والحية واعترض وأجيب بما مر في سورة البقرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r6.claim: The apparent sequence has God immediately rebuke Adam for his act, without intervening event.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r6.anchor: والظاهر من النظم الكريم أن آدم عليه السلام عاجله ربه سبحانه بالعتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r7.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r7.claim: Al-Ghazālī’s report says the forbidden tree alone caused bodily waste in Paradise, leading Adam to seek a place to relieve himself before descent; al-Ālūsī says the report is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r7.anchor: حجة الاسلام الغزالي أنه عليه السلام لما أكل من الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r8.speaker: محمد بن قيس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r8.claim: Muḥammad ibn Qays relates that Adam blamed Eve, she blamed the serpent, and the serpent blamed Iblīs; God assigned Eve monthly bleeding, the serpent to crawl and be struck in the face, and cursed Iblīs.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس قال : إنه عليه السلام لما أكل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r1.claim: The enmity clause may be a simultaneous or prospective circumstantial clause; some grammarians take it as a new sentence answering how the descent leaves them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r1.anchor: في موضع الحال من فاعل اهبطوا وهي حال مقارنة أو مقدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r2.claim: The enmity is straightforward if Satan is included; if only Adam and Eve are addressed, it can extend to descendants, or mean mutual oppression through Satan’s misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r2.anchor: على تقدير التخصيص بآدم وحواء عليهما السلام فقد قيل إنه باعتبار

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r3.claim: Mustaqarr means settling or a place of settlement; it may also mean earthly dominion established for them and use permitted, though that reading is less apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r3.anchor: أي استقرار أو موضع استقرار فهو اما مصدر ميمي أو اسم مكان

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r4.claim: The word could mean a time of settlement, but that does not fit because it would repeat ‘until a time.’
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r4.anchor: اسم زمان إلا أنه غير محتمل هنا لأنه يتكرر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r5.claim: Earthly enjoyment lasts until death or resurrection; dwelling in the grave may count as enjoyment in earth, and ‘for you’ may refer to humankind collectively.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r5.anchor: يريد به وقت الموت وقيل القيامة وتجعل السكنى في القبر تمتعا في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r6.claim: The prepositional phrase may modify ‘enjoyment,’ both it and ‘settlement’ by attraction, or an omitted adjective clause for ‘enjoyment.’
ALUSI-FULL:v8p102#2/r6.anchor: والظرف قيل متعلق بمتاع أو به وبمستقر على التنازع

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r1.claim: The address includes Adam, Eve, and their descendants, or Adam and Eve together with Iblīs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r1.anchor: الخطاب لآدم وحواء وذريتهما، أو لهما ولإبليس

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r2.claim: The command is repeated with Iblīs included so that their permanent companionship is understood; the speech is reported in separate parts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r2.anchor: كرر الأمر له تبعا ليعلم أنهم قرناء أبدا وأخبر عما قال لهم متفرقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r3.claim: The phrase is circumstantial: they descend in a state of mutual enmity.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r4.claim: Mustaqarr means a place where people settle.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r5.claim: Matāʿ means enjoyment or provision for use.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r5.anchor: ولكم فى الأرض مستقر } استقرار أي موضع استقرار. { ومتع } وتمتع

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:24/r6.claim: The period lasts until each person's appointed lifespan ends.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r20.claim: The descent sends them to the abode of struggle, contest, and conflict.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r20.anchor: أي إلى دار المجاهده والمقارعة والمناكدة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r21.claim: Adam, Eve, and their descendants are enemies of Iblīs and his descendants, while some human offspring will also be enemies to one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r21.anchor: أي أنتما ومن ولدتماه أعداء إبليس

BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r22.claim: There is no rescue from this conflict except by following the guidance of reason, supported by revelation; the warning calls for constant vigilance even after repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r22.anchor: ولا خلاص إلا باتباع ما منحتكم من هدى العقل وما أنزلت إليكم من تأييده بالنقل وفي ذلك تهديد صادع

BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r23.claim: Earth here means the earth as a whole, and mustaqarr is a place of settlement, such as the plains.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r24.claim: The worldly provision lasts until their lifespans expire and then until the world itself ends.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p17/r24.anchor: انقضاء آجالكم ثم انقضاء أجل الدنيا

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r1.claim: God addresses Adam, Eve, their descendants, and Iblīs with the command to descend.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r1.anchor: {قال} الله تعالى {اهبطوا} خطاب لآدم وحواء وذريتهما أولهما ولإبليس

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r2.claim: They descend as enemies: Iblīs is innately hostile, like a scorpion that stings or a wolf that steals; he resented Adam's succession and lost leadership among the angels.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r2.anchor: {بعضكم لبعض عدو} جملة حالية من فاعل اهبطوا

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r3.claim: Humans are commanded to oppose Iblīs because a son opposes his father's enemy.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r3.anchor: وأمرنا بمعاداة إبليس لأن الابن يعادي عدو أبيه

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r4.claim: Mustaqarr means a place of settlement and rest.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r4.anchor: {ولكم فى الارض مستقر} (قرار كاهى وآرام جايى)

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r5.claim: Matāʿ means enjoyment and benefit until the end of their appointed lifespans; Adam grieved, thinking he would not return to Paradise.

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī depicts Adam as once honored above creation, then stripped of his garments and ease after one sin; this warns how much worse many sins may be for us.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.anchor: قال الإمام القشيري : ونعم ما قال : أصبح آدم عليه السلام محسود الملائكة

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's couplet laments longing for union while one's soul remains bound by destiny to separation.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.anchor: قال الحافظ : ه كونه دعوىء وصلت كنم بجانكه شدست

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.claim: Divine decree governs everyone, whether prophet or saint.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.anchor: وقضاء الله تعالى يجري على كل أحد نبيا كان أو وليا

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r10.claim: Adam ate from the tree of love and entered a trial of separation, then was promised discovery after loss; spiritual ascent followed his outward descent.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r10.anchor: واعلم : أن آدم تناول من شجرة المحبة حقيقة فوقع في شبكة المحنة

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r11.claim: The tree of bare knowledge must not be approached without unveiling and direct witnessing: its possessor remains veiled from the fruits of reality; seekers should aspire to witnessing and God can complete the journey in the isthmus after death.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r11.anchor: وشجرة العلم المجرد منهي عن أن يقربها أحد بدون المكاشفة

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r12.claim: One should also avoid the tree of self-directed planning and trust the decree; prayer's standing signifies primordial surrender, bowing signifies submission to eternal ordering, and prostration signifies complete effacement of both.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r12.anchor: وأيضا لا ينبغي لأحد أن يقرب من شجرة التدبير فإن التقدير كاف لكل غني وفقير

DURR-FULL:v3p432/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p432/r9.speaker: حبر تيما
DURR-FULL:v3p432/r9.claim: A Jewish scholar answers Ibn Abbas that human settlement is above the earth, in the womb, below the earth, and wherever one ultimately goes, Paradise or Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p432/r9.anchor: حبر تيما حدثني عن قوله {ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين} فقال: هو مستقره فوق الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r1.speaker: رجاء بن أبي سلمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r1.claim: He describes Adam descending with hands on his knees and head bowed, while Iblis descended with fingers interlocked and head raised toward the sky.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r1.anchor: عن رجاء بن ابى سلمة قال : اهبط ادم يديه على ركبتيه مطاطئا راسه ، واهبط ابليس مشبكا بين اصابعه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r2.claim: He says Adam descended at al-Ṣafā and Eve at al-Marwa.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : اهبط ادم بالصفا ، وحواء بالمروة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r3.claim: He says Adam first descended to Dahna, a region in India.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان اول ما اهبط الله ادم إلى الأرض اهبطه بدحناء ارض بالهند

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r4.claim: In another report he places Adam's descent at a place called Dahna between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قال : اهبط ادم عليه السلام إلى ارض يقال لها دحنا ، بين مكة والطائف

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r5.claim: He says Adam landed in India, Eve in Jeddah, Iblis in Dast Maysan near Basra, and the serpent in Isfahan.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال : هبط ادم بالهند ، وحواء بجدة ، وابليس بدست ميسان

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r6.claim: He says Adam landed in India carrying leaves from Paradise; perfume trees grew from them, explaining India's perfumes, and Adam had kept the leaves in grief at leaving Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r6.anchor: عن السدى : قال : قال الله : اهبطوا منها جميعا فهبطوا : فنزل ادم بالهند وانزل معه بقبضة من ورق الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r7.speaker: النسري بن يحيى
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r7.claim: He says Adam descended from Paradise with seeds, and Iblis laid a hand on them so that the seeds he touched lost their benefit.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r7.anchor: عن النسري بن يحيى قال : اهبط ادم من الجنة ومعه البذور ، فوضع ابليس عليها يده

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r8.claim: He identifies the parties as Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1454#2/r8.anchor: من سمع ابن عباس يقول : اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو قال : ادم وحواء وابليس والحية

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r1.claim: He glosses the place of settlement as the graves; Ibn Masʿud and al-Sadi are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : ولكم في الأرض مستقر قال : مستقر ، القبور

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r2.claim: He says people have a place of settlement both above the earth and beneath it.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : ولكم في الأرض مستقر قال : مستقر فوق الأرض ومستقر تحت الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r3.speaker: أبو العالية عن الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r3.claim: He links the statement about settlement on earth with the verse saying that God made the earth a bed for you.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r3.anchor: عن الربيع عن ابى العالية في قوله : ولكم في الأرض مستقر قال : هو قوله : الذين جعل لكم الأرض فراشا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r4.claim: He glosses the provision as sustenance lasting until death.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r4.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : ومتاع إلى حين يقول : بلاغ إلى الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r5.claim: He glosses the appointed term as life.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس : ومتاع إلى حين قال : الحياة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r6.claim: He says the provision lasts until a person reaches either Paradise or Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r6.anchor: عن كريب عن ابن عباس : قوله : ومتاع إلى حين قال : حتى يصير إلى الجنة أو إلى النار

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r7.claim: He glosses the term as an endpoint that cannot be apprehended.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1455/r7.anchor: قال عكرمة ومتاع إلى حين قال : الحين الذي لا يدرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.claim: The clause about having a settled place on earth is coordinated with the preceding clause that some are enemies to others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1.anchor: وعطفت جملة : { ولكم في الأرض مستقر } على جملة : { بعضكم لبعض عدو }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.claim: مستقر is a mimetic verbal noun meaning remaining or staying; Ibn Ashur points to the same word in two other verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2.anchor: والمستقر مصدر ميمي والاستقرار هو المكث وقد تقدم القول فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.claim: Some exegetes took the settled place to mean burial, but Ibn Ashur rejects this because enjoyment is mentioned and jinn and devils are not buried in the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3.anchor: وليس المراد به الدفن كما فسر به بعض المفسرين لأن قوله ومتاع يصد عن ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.claim: متاع and تمتع mean gaining nonlasting pleasures and desires; متاع can also denote the things from which one benefits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4.anchor: والمتاع والتمتع : نيل الملذات والمرغوبات غير الدائمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.claim: حين means a period, long or short; it is indefinite here because its duration varies among kinds and individuals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5.anchor: والحين المدة من الزمن ، طويلة أو قصيرة ، وقد نكر هنا ولم يحدد لاختلاف مقداره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r6.claim: The period is the life in which a being can perceive pleasures and persist as a living self; this divinely determined term ends with life, ending settled existence and enjoyment, and is neither favor nor punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الزمن المقارن لحالة الحياة والإدراك هو المسمى بالأجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r1.speaker: أبو صالح والسدي والطبري وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r1.claim: Abu Salih, al-Suddi, al-Tabari, and others say those commanded to descend were Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r1.anchor: قال أبو صالح والسدي والطبري وغيرهم: هي لآدم وحواء وإبليس والحية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r2.claim: Another group takes the addressees to be Adam and his descendants together with Iblis and his descendants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r2.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هي مخاطبة لآدم وذريته وإبليس وذريته.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that view because the descendants did not yet exist; making the command conditional on their future existence is unsuitable here, since descent would not itself affect them as prayer or fasting would.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف لعدمهم في ذلك الوقت، فإن قيل خاطبهم وأمرهم بشرط الوجود فذلك يبعد في هذه النازلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r4.claim: The command to descend in 20:123 addresses Adam and Iblis, as shown by the verse's explanation that they are enemies to one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r4.anchor: وأما قوله في آية أخرى اهبطا [طه: 123] فهي مخاطبة لآدم وإبليس بدليل بيانه العداوة بينهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r5.claim: The singular noun ʿaduww is used with plural meaning, as in the Arabic expressions qawm ʿaduww and qawm ṣadīq.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r5.anchor: وعدو فرد بمعنى الجمع، تقول قوم عدو وقوم صديق.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r6.claim: The cited anonymous verse uses ṣadīq for a plural group, illustrating singular-form words with plural reference.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r6.anchor: لعمري لئن كنتم على النأي والغنى ... بكم مثل ما بي إنكم لصديق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r7.claim: Hostility toward snakes is well known.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r8.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet's statement that Muslims have not made peace with snakes since they fought them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r8.anchor: وروى قتادة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «ما سالمناهن منذ حاربناهن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r9.claim: Ibn Umar says that whoever leaves snakes alone is not one of the community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r9.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر: «من تركهن فليس منا» ، وقالت عائشة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r10.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r10.claim: Aisha says that anyone who leaves a snake out of fear of its revenge incurs the curse of God, angels, and all people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r10.anchor: من ترك حية خشية من ثأرها فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r11.claim: The Prophet said that jinn in Medina had become Muslims; a house snake should be warned three times, then killed if it remains, since it is an unbeliever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r11.anchor: وقول النبي عليه السلام: إن جنا بالمدينة قد أسلموا فمن رأى من هذه الحيات شيئا في بيته فليحرج عليه ثلاثا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r12.claim: Mustaqarr broadly includes both the span of earthly life and residence in graves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r12.anchor: مستقر لفظ عام لزمن الحياة ولزمن الإقامة في القبور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r13.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r13.claim: Abu al-Aliyya takes mustaqarr to mean life on earth and links it to the earth made as a resting place in 2:22.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r13.anchor: وبزمن الحياة فسر أبو العالية وقال: هي كقوله الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا [البقرة: 22]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas takes mustaqarr to mean residence in the graves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r14.anchor: وبالإقامة في القبور فسر ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r15.claim: The broad meaning also fits 77:25, where the earth gathers the living and the dead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p387/r15.anchor: فهي كقوله: ألم نجعل الأرض كفاتا أحياء وأمواتا [المرسلات: 25]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r1.speaker: رواية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r1.claim: Reports place Adam's descent in India and Eve's in Jeddah, then derive the place names Mina, Arafat, and Jamʿ from his longing, recognition, and meeting with her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r1.anchor: وروي أن آدم عليه السلام أهبط بالهند وحواء بجدة، وتمناها بمنى، وعرف حقيقة أمرها بعرفة، ولقيها بجمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r2.speaker: رواية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r2.claim: Reports place Iblis's descent in Maysan, Basra, or Egypt, where he bred; Ibn Umar is quoted as saying Iblis spread his rich carpet there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r2.anchor: وأهبط إبليس بميسان وقيل بالبصرة وقيل بمصر فباض فيها وفرخ، قال ابن عمر وبسط إبليس فيها عبقريه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r3.speaker: صالح مولى التؤمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r3.claim: In a report from some books, Satan's dwelling is bathhouses, his meeting place markets, his amusement flutes, his food what lacks God's name, his drink intoxicants, and his messengers lusts, with women as snares.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r3.anchor: وذكر صالح مولى التؤمة قال في بعض الكتب لما أهبط إبليس قال رب أين مسكني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r4.speaker: رواية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r4.claim: A report places the serpent's descent in Isfahan.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r5.speaker: رواية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r5.claim: A report says the serpent once had legs like a camel and was punished by being made to glide on its belly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r5.anchor: وروي أنها كانت ذات قوائم كالبعير فعوقبت بأن ردت تنساب على بطنها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r6.speaker: رواية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r6.claim: A report says Adam learned ironworking and farming after descent, then labored through every stage from plowing and watering to baking and cooking before he ate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r6.anchor: وروي أن آدم لما أهبط إلى شقاء الدنيا علم صنعة الحديد ثم علم الحرث فحرث وسقى وحصد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r7.speaker: رواية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r7.claim: A report tells Eve that, as the tree bled, she would bleed monthly and bear pregnancy and childbirth painfully; her lament was imposed on her and her descendants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r7.anchor: وروي أن حواء قيل لها يا حواء كما دميت الشجرة فأنت تدمين في كل شهر وأنت لا تحمل إلا كرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says he has shortened these many transmitted details because the verse's wording does not require them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r8.anchor: وفي هذه القصة من الأنباء كثير اختصرتها إذ لا يقتضيها اللفظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r14.claim: Matāʿ is enjoyment and the acquisition of benefits; here it belongs to each person during life, though grave residence might in some way count as enjoyment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r14.anchor: شخص شخص، في زمن الحياة اللهم إلا أن يقدر سكنى القبر متاعا بوجه ما، و «المتاع» التمتع والنيل من الفوائد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r15.claim: The term extends collectively until the Hour, but individually until each person's appointed term and death; ḥīn is an unspecified time in Arabic usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r15.anchor: وإلى حين هو بحسب الجملة قيام الساعة، وبحسب مفرد بلوغ الأجل والموت، والحين في كلام العرب الوقت غير معين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r1.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r1.claim: Some say the command to descend addressed Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent; others omit the serpent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r1.anchor: قيل: المراد بالخطاب في {اهبطوا} آدم، وحواء، وإبليس، والحية. ومنهم من لم يذكر الحية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r2.claim: The central enmity is between Adam and Iblis, as the descent command addresses the two in 20:123; Eve follows Adam, and the serpent—if its mention is authentic—follows Iblis.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r2.anchor: والعمدة في العداوة آدم وإبليس؛ ولهذا قال تعالى في سورة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r3.claim: Commentators’ accounts of where each person landed reduce to Israelite reports of uncertain reliability; if such locations mattered religiously or worldly, God or His Messenger would have stated them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر المفسرون الأماكن التي هبط فيها كل منهم، ويرجع حاصل تلك الأخبار إلى الإسرائيليات، والله أعلم بصحتها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r4.claim: The earth provides settlement and lifetimes fixed until known terms, decreed and recorded in the first book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r4.anchor: أي: قرار وأعمار مضروبة إلى آجال معلومة، قد جرى بها القلم، وأحصاها القدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets mustaqarr as the graves.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399/r6.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbas takes mustaqarr as the earth’s surface and what lies beneath it.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.claim: The plural reports Adam and Eve descending together with their separation, although the wording is an imperative.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r1.anchor: إن خرج مخرج الأمر , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r2.claim: The plural addressees are Adam, Eve, and the serpent, making them a group.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r3.claim: The plural addressees are Adam, Eve, and the whispering temptation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.claim: Adam descended in India on Mount Wāsim, Eve at Jeddah, and the serpent at Isfahan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r4.anchor: فهبط آدم بأرض الهند على جبل يقال له واسم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.claim: One reported location for Iblis's descent is al-Ubulla.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r5.anchor: وفي مهبط إبليس قولان . أحدهما بالأبلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r6.claim: A second reported location for Iblis's descent is al-Madār.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.claim: A report says they remained in the Garden until nine hours of Friday had passed, then were sent out.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r7.anchor: قيل أسكنهما الجنة لئلا ساعات خلت من يوم الجمعة , وأخرجهما لتسع ساعات خلت من ذلك اليوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r8.claim: Mustaqarr can mean the act of settling or the place of settlement; Abu Salih gives the latter gloss.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r8.anchor: أما المستقر ففيه وجهان : أحدهما : أنه فعل الاستقرار

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r9.claim: Matāʿ means the worldly goods and benefits that people enjoy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r9.anchor: وأما المتاع فهو المنتفع به من عروض الدنيا التي يستمتع بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r10.claim: The term means until the world's end; its duration is indefinite, can be long or short, and usually suggests a long time, as the cited poem illustrates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p211#2/r10.anchor: والحين وقت مجهول القدر ينطلق على طويل الزمان وقصيره وإن كان موضوعا في الأغلب للتكثير

MUQATIL:7:22-24/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r7.claim: Those commanded to descend from the garden are Adam, Eve, Iblīs, and the serpent.
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r7.anchor: وأوحى إليهما: { قال اهبطوا } من الجنة، آدم، وحواء، وإبليس، والحية،

MUQATIL:7:22-24/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r8.claim: Iblīs is an enemy to Adam and Eve, and they are enemies to him.
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r8.anchor: { بعضكم لبعض عدو } ، يقول: إبليس لهما عدو، وهما إبليس عدو،

MUQATIL:7:22-24/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r9.claim: Earth is their place of settlement and provision until the end of their lifespans; Iblīs remains until the first trumpet blast.
MUQATIL:7:22-24/r9.anchor: { ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين } [آية: 24]، يعني إلى منتهى آجالكم، وإبليس في النفخة الأولى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r1.claim: The plural command addresses Adam and Eve because Iblis had descended earlier; alternatively, Iblis first went up to heaven and all then descended together.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r1.anchor: الخطاب لآدم وحواء بلفظ الجمع لأن إبليس هبط من قبل ويحتمل أنه هبط إلى السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r2.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial state meaning they are enemies: Iblis opposes them and they oppose him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r2.anchor: فى موضع الحال أى متعادين يعاديهما إبليس ويعاديانه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r3.claim: Mustaqarr means either stability or a place of stability; matāʿ is enjoyment of livelihood.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r3.anchor: في الأرض مستقر ﴾ استقرار أو موضع استقرار ﴿ ومتاع ﴾ وانتفاع بعيش

NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r4.claim: The appointed period lasts until your lifespans end.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r4.anchor: إلى انقضاء آجالكم وعن ثابت البنانى لما أهبط آدم عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r5.speaker: ثابت البنانى
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r5.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī reports that near Adam's death, angels gathered around; Eve circled them, and Adam told her to leave them, saying his fate had come through her. The angels washed, perfumed, shrouded, buried him in Serendib, and taught his descendants the practice.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p7#4/r5.anchor: عن ثابت البنانى لما أهبط آدم عليه السلام وحضرته الوفاة وأحاطت به الملائكة فجعلت حواء تدور حولهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:22-24/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:22-24/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:22-24/r22.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the meaning of the command to descend was discussed earlier, along with the rest of the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:22-24/r22.anchor: ومعنى قوله: { قال اهبطوا } تقدم أيضا إلى آخر الآية.

RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says this account, explained in al-Baqara, implies Adam committed a grave sin, but resolves the question by placing it before prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية مفسرة في سورة البقرة ، وقد ذكرنا هناك أن هذه الآية تدل على صدور الذنب العظيم من آدم عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r2.claim: God cast Iblis down from his rank into the curse, while Adam was sent from his place and then overtaken by mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r2.anchor: أهبطهم ، ولكنه أهبط إبليس عن رتبته فوقع في اللعنة ، وأهبط آدم عن بقعته فتداركته الرحمة

QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r3.claim: Adam lost the abode of honor but retained his rank of virtue; Qushayri cites God’s later choosing him as proof.
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r3.anchor: لم يخرج آدم عليه السلام من رتبة الفضيلة وإن أخرج عن دار الكرامة ، فلذلك قال الله تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r4.claim: Iblis was expelled from both his spiritual state and rank and never recovered from that fall.
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r4.anchor: فإنه أخرج من الحالة والرتبة ؛ فلم ينتعش قط عن تلك السقطة

QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r5.claim: The earthly dwelling applies generally, but the temporary enjoyment is directed specifically to Iblis.
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r5.anchor: { ولكم فى الأرض مستقر } هذا عام { ومتاع إلى حين } : أراد به إبليس على الخصوص

QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r6.claim: Earthly life brings alternating conditions: hardship and ease, good and evil, life and death, victory and loss.
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r6.anchor: يتعاقب عليهم تفاوت الأطوار ، فمن عسر ومن يسر ، ومن خير ومن شر ، ومن حياة ومن موت ، ومن ظفر ومن فوت

QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r7.claim: God conceals people from the visible causes of harm and equips them with benefits by which they can ward off many harms.
QUSHAYRI:v1p329/r7.anchor: سترناكم عن الأسباب الظاهرة ، ويسرنا لكم ما تدفعون به صنوف المضار عنكم بما مكنا لكم من وجوه المنافع

TAB-FULL:v10p117/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r1.claim: God tells Adam, Eve, Iblīs, and the serpent to descend from heaven to earth, where they are enemies to one another.
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r1.anchor: عن السدي: {اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو} [الأعراف: 24] ، قال ": فلعن الحية، وقطع قوائمها، وتركها تمشي على بطنها

TAB-FULL:v10p117/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says God cursed the serpent, removed its legs, made it crawl on its belly and live on dust, then sent Adam, Eve, Iblīs, and the serpent down.
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو} [الأعراف: 24] ، قال ": فلعن الحية، وقطع قوائمها، وتركها تمشي على بطنها

TAB-FULL:v10p117/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r3.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ identifies those addressed as Adam, Eve, and the serpent.
TAB-FULL:v10p117/r3.anchor: عن أبي صالح: {اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو} [الأعراف: 24] قال: «آدم وحواء والحية»

TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r1.claim: The earth is a place of residence and a spread-out resting place for Adam, Eve, Iblīs, and the serpent.
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية، في قوله: {ولكم في الأرض مستقر} [البقرة: 36] قال: هو قوله: {الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا} [البقرة: 22]

TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya connects the phrase with God's making the earth a bed in 2:22.
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية، في قوله: {ولكم في الأرض مستقر} [البقرة: 36] قال: هو قوله: {الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا} [البقرة: 22]

TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r3.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās interprets their settled place as the graves.
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولكم في الأرض مستقر} [البقرة: 36] قال: «القبور»

TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the statement is general: people reside on earth during life and inside it after death, not only in one state.
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r4.anchor: ولهم فيها مستقر في حياتهم على ظهرها وبعد وفاتهم في بطنها

TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r5.claim: He supports this inclusive reading with the earth described as containing the living and the dead in 77:25–26.
TAB-FULL:v10p117#2/r5.anchor: كما قال جل ثناؤه: {ألم نجعل الأرض كفاتا} [المرسلات: 25] ، {أحياء وأمواتا} [المرسلات: 26]

TAB-FULL:v10p118/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r1.claim: The provision on earth lasts until the world's end, the “time” mentioned here.
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ومتاع إلى حين} [الأعراف: 24] قال: «إلى يوم القيامة وإلى انقطاع الدنيا»

TAB-FULL:v10p118/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “until a time” as lasting to the Day of Resurrection and the end of the world.
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ومتاع إلى حين} [الأعراف: 24] قال: «إلى يوم القيامة وإلى انقطاع الدنيا»

TAB-FULL:v10p118/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r3.claim: Ḥīn means a period whose precise measure is unknown; a cited poem's “a time, no time” illustrates its indeterminate duration.
TAB-FULL:v10p118/r3.anchor: مجهول القدر، يدل على ذلك قول الشاعر

TABRISI:7:22-25/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:22-25/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:22-25/r14.claim: The descent and enmity statement was explained earlier in the commentary on al-Baqara.
TABRISI:7:22-25/r14.anchor: قد مر تفسيره في سورة البقرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:23-24/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:23-24/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:23-24/r1.claim: The place of settlement is a place of dwelling.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:23-24/r1.anchor: { قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر } موضع قرار.

ELMALILI:7:23-25/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:23-25/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:23-25/r6.claim: The descent assigns them an earthly dwelling and provision for a limited time, amid enmity among them.
ELMALILI:7:23-25/r6.anchor: ve size arzda bir vakte kadar bir istikrar ve temettu‘var

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r1.claim: Adam and Eve repented after recognizing their sin; God accepted their repentance, as 2:37 says, then sent them to the world as a place of testing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r1.anchor: Bakara sûresinde (2/37) belirtildiği üzere Allah da onların tövbelerini kabul etmiş ve onları imtihan yurdu olan dünyaya göndermiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r3.claim: Together with 2:36, 2:38, and 20:123, these verses show Adam and Eve were expelled from Paradise because of their sin, an event that shaped humanity’s fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r3.anchor: gerek bu âyetten gerekse ilgili diğer âyetlerden (bk. Bakara 2/36, 38; Tâhâ 20/123), Âdem ile eşinin, işledikleri günahın bir sonucu olmak üzere cennetten çıkarıldıkları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r4.claim: The Torah’s account that Adam and Eve also faced other hardships is absent from the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r4.anchor: Fakat Âdem ile Havvâ’nın bu yüzden daha başka zahmetlere de mâruz kalacaklarının bildirildiği yolunda Tevrat’ta verilen bilgiler (Tekvîn, 3/16-19) Kur’an’da geçmemektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r5.claim: The enmity may mean the enduring conflict between humans and Satan, quarrels between spouses, and conflicts among Adam and Eve’s descendants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r5.anchor: Burada anılan düşmanlığın, hem insanoğlu ile şeytan arasındaki ebedî düşmanlığı hem karı-koca arasındaki çekişmeleri hem de Âdem ve Havvâ’nın soyu arasındaki çatışmaları ifade ettiği düşünülebilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r6.claim: One interpretation includes Iblis among those told to descend, since Paradise, described in the Qur’an as the abode of peace, cannot contain enmity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r6.anchor: Bu sebeple onlara –bir yoruma göre İblîs de kastedilerek– “İnin oradan!..” buyurulmuştur. Çünkü Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in “dârüsselâm” (barış yurdu) diye tanımladığı cennette düşmanlık olamazdı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r7.claim: Adam and Eve’s initial purity was instinctive rather than chosen, so although not bad, it carried no moral value.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r7.anchor: Kuşkusuz Âdem ve Havvâ’nın cennette saf ve günahsız olmaları iradeye dayanmadığı için –kötü bir durum sayılmasa bile– ahlâkî bir değer de ifade etmiyor, sadece içgüdüsel bir karakter taşıyordu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r8.claim: The prohibition on the tree brought freedom of choice: Adam and Eve moved from instinctive to deliberate action, recognized wrongdoing, sought pardon, and were forgiven.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r8.anchor: böylece insanlığın atası ve annesi, yasaklanmış ağaçtan yeme olayında içgüdüsel davranmaktan bilinçli ve iradeli davranma aşamasına geçmişler; kötülüklerinin farkına vararak af dilemişler ve bağışlanmışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.claim: The move from first sin and expulsion marks humanity’s moral rise into a free, accountable kind of being able to err, repent, and consciously choose goodness, not a moral decline.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.anchor: ilk günahla başlayan ve cennetten çıkarılma ile devam eden süreç, insanlık için ahlâkî bakımdan bir düşüşü değil, bir yükselişi

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r8.claim: The address appears to include Adam, his wife, and Iblis; their mutual enmity is seen in their differing natures, and the earthly dwelling and provision last until worldly life ends.

THALABI:v4p225/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p225/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p225/r3.claim: The earth is the place where they dwell and enjoy provision for a limited term; there they live, die, and are brought forth.
THALABI:v4p225/r3.anchor: قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين قال فيها تحيون

BURHAN:v2p178/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p178/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p178/r9.claim: A strained argument combines verses to claim animals have the same religious obligations as humans; the author rejects that inference.
BURHAN:v2p178/r9.anchor: والثاني ان يلفق بين اثنين كقول من زعم تكليف الحيوانات
